'''Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Kami''' (天目一箇神) is a deity in [[Japanese mythology]] associated with [[:en:ironworking|ironworking]] and [[:en:blacksmithing|blacksmithing]].
== Overview ==
Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Kami appears in ''{{ill|Kogo Shūi|en|Kogo Shūi|qid=Q531555|lt=Kogo Shūi|1=Kogo Shūi}}'', ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', and ''{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|qid=Q11498726|lt=Harima no Kuni Fudoki|1=Harima no Kuni Fudoki}}''. alternate_name include '''Ame-no-Mahitotsune-no-Mikoto''' (天之麻比止都禰命), '''Ame-no-Kushima-Hitotsu-no-Mikoto''' (天久斯麻比止都命), '''Amatsu-Mara''' (天津麻羅), and several others.<ref name=":0">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/816099 「御上神社沿革考 : 近江国野洲郡三上村鎮座」 大谷治作 編 / 出版: 太田治左衛門 / 出版年月日: 明32.2]（National Diet Library Digital Collections）</ref> The deity is considered the origin of ''{{ill|Hyottoko|en|Hyottoko|qid=Q795293|lt=Hyottoko|1=Hyottoko}}'' (fire man).
According to the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku|1=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}''<ref>中田憲信「東国諸国造（天津彦根命裔）」『諸系譜』第一冊。</ref>, Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Kami is a child of [[Amatsuhikone|Amatsu-Hikone-no-Mikoto]]. Descendants include the {{ill|Inbe clan|en|Inbe clan|qid=Q8189229|lt=Imibe clan|1=Inbe clan}} of Tsukushi and Ise Provinces, the Sugada chiefs of Yamashiro Province, and other clans.<ref>『新撰姓氏録』</ref><ref>『先代旧事本紀』 巻第十 国造本紀</ref>
== Analysis ==
As the god of blacksmithing, Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Kami is often identified with {{ill|Ama-Tsu-Mara|en|Ama-Tsu-Mara|qid=Q10940368|lt=Ama-Tsu-Mara|1=Ama-Tsu-Mara}}, a figure appearing in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}''. The name "Mahitotsu" (one eye) refers to the blacksmith's practice of closing one eye while gauging metal temperature or a common occupational hazard among smiths.
The deity is also mentioned in the ''{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|qid=Q11498726|lt=Harima no Kuni Fudoki|1=Harima no Kuni Fudoki}}'', where he appears as the father of a child borne by the local goddess Michinushi-Hime. This narrative is interpreted as symbolizing the integration of agricultural and metallurgical societies. At the {{ill|Ameichi Shrine|ja|天目一神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ameichi Shrine|qq=}} in present-day {{ill|Nishiwaki|en|Nishiwaki|qid=Q17124933|lt=Nishiwaki|1=Nishiwaki}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture|1=Hyōgo Prefecture}}, he is venerated as the god of ironworking.
== Ichimoku Ren ==
{{ill|Ichimoku Ren|ja|一目連|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichimoku Ren|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天目一箇神|1=Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10016750}} (One-Eyed Ren) is the deity enshrined at {{ill|Tado Taisha|en|Tado Taisha|qid=Q116140|lt=Tado Taisha|1=Tado Taisha}}'s Ichimoku Shrine. While often equated with Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Kami, Ichimoku Ren originated as a {{ill|Ryujin (disambiguation)|en|Ryujin (disambiguation)|qid=Q123290706|lt=Ryujin (disambiguation)|1=Ryujin (disambiguation)}} associated with weather control. Over time, the two deities merged.
Ichimoku Ren is revered as a wind god. During the Edo period, sailors prayed to him for protection from storms. {{ill|Kunio Yanagita|en|Kunio Yanagita|qid=Q971687|lt=Kunio Yanagita|1=Kunio Yanagita}} theorized that seafarers derived this faith from observing [[Tado Mountain]]’s weather patterns.<ref>『一目小僧その他』</ref>
The ''{{ill|Wakan Sansai Zue|en|Wakan Sansai Zue|qid=Q1135803|lt=Wakan Sansai Zue|1=Wakan Sansai Zue}}'' records, "Violent winds in Ise, Owari, Mino, and Hida are attributed to Ichimoku Ren, believed to be a divine wind."<ref>『[{{NDLDC|898160/69|qq=}} 和漢三才図会巻第三 天部 颶]』</ref>
*
According to traditions of the {{ill|Okinaga Clan|ja|息長氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okinaga Clan|qq=}} {{ill|Ame-no-Mikage-no-Kami|ja|天之御影神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Mikage no Kami|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|ja|天之御影神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|qq=}} may be the same god.
